title: Traffic on the roof of the world
text: The summit of Everest now {{1}} queues. In May 2019, photographs showed climbers {{2}} in a line up a ridge at 8,500 metres, waiting hours in the death zone for a rope to clear; eleven died that season, most of them in the crowds rather than on the rock. The mountain has become a {{3}}: the southeast route is fixed with ropes and ladders each spring, commercial expeditions {{4}} clients of varying experience, and the permit fee — eleven thousand dollars — buys a place in the queue, not the ability to survive it. Veteran guides {{5}} that experience thresholds have slipped, and that some clients cannot {{6}} their own oxygen equipment. Nepal benefits: Everest {{7}} a meaningful share of national tourism income, and restrictions are politically costly. Fixes under discussion {{8}} from requiring recent high-altitude ascents to capping permits — but the deeper constraint is simple: the weather window is short, and everyone wants the same two weeks in May.

gaps.explanation: 'the summit now hosts queues' — has them on it; hoist = lift, hound = pursue relentlessly.
'climbers shuffling in a line' — dragging their feet slowly forward; shudder = tremble.
'the mountain has become a staircase' — fixed ropes and ladders turn it into one; stile = steps over a fence.
'expeditions escort clients of varying experience' — accompany and look after them; evacuate = remove from danger.
'guides complain that thresholds have slipped' — voice their objection; comply takes 'with', combust = catch fire.
'cannot operate their own oxygen equipment' — work it correctly; orchestrate = arrange a complex event.
'Everest generates a meaningful share of income' — brings it into existence; germinate = begin to grow, garnish = decorate food.
'fixes range from requiring ascents to capping permits' — 'range from X to Y' is the fixed pattern; diverge = draw apart.
